$comment: Seed list for the browse-by-industry directory. NOT validated. Every entry must pass the validation script before it ships. tier=confirmed means a jobs.ashbyhq.com/<slug> URL was observed. tier=named means a source names the company as an Ashby user but the slug is unresolved. tier=candidate means both Ashby membership and the slug are unverified; expect roughly 15-25 percent of candidates to be on Ashby, since Greenhouse and Lever hold most of the rest of this market. Slugs are often not guessable (RAD Amplify is rad-intel, edu.fyi is fyi), so probe slugCandidates in order, keep the first 200, and fall back to scraping the careers page at domainCandidates for anything that misses.
$mergeGuidance: Counts below are pre-validation and will shrink a lot. After validation, drop or merge any industry left under minCompaniesPerIndustry. The threshold is 3, not 6: the argument that a chip returning two companies is worse than no chip holds at 2 and not at 5, and dropping a label to avoid a small chip solves a display problem by deleting data. Chips show their count, so 'Gaming 3' sets its own expectation.
$renameGuidance: industryRenames are applied unconditionally, before any threshold logic, unlike suggestedMerges which only fire below minCompaniesPerIndustry. Use them to relabel a category, not to rescue a thin one. Transportation and Logistics were two thin chips splitting a coherent category where neither label fit the other's members: project44 is supply chain visibility rather than transportation, and Wayve is autonomous driving rather than logistics. One chip is both more accurate and better to browse.
